We will also continue advancing our earlier proposal to strengthen the BWC through establishing an international agency for biological security. Distinguished delegates, peace and stability are a prerequisite for sustainable development. We stand firmly for diplomacy and dialogue and against the escalation of tension and the use of force. We remain deeply concerned about the Ukrainian crisis, which continues to take lives, erode global trust, and undermine international security. Even the most difficult conflicts must, ultimately, be resolved through diplomacy and negotiation. Beyond the tragic loss of life, Kazakhstan strongly condemns the repeated drone attacks against Kazakh crude oil export infrastructure, including against commercial vessels in the Black Sea basin. Such incidents endanger civilian navigation, disrupt international trade, and threaten the stability of global energy supplies. We call on all parties to uphold international law and take all necessary measures to protect critical infrastructure and ensure the safety and continuity of civilian commerce. Political and diplomatic means remain the only viable path towards ending hostilities and achieving sustainable resolution of the Middle East crisis. The ongoing escalation carries serious implications for regional and international peace and security, as well as for economic stability, transport connectivity, and energy security. Just as lasting peace in the Middle East requires an independent, sovereign, and viable state of Palestine living side by side with Israel in peace and security, we support the new the New York Declaration as a framework for tangible, time-bound, and irreversible steps toward this two-state solution. My country stands ready to support every effort aimed at maintaining unimpeded humanitarian assistance, protection of civilians, and recovery of Gaza. Kazakhstan's calls for the full and good faith implementation of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and Security Council Resolution 2803. As a member of the Board of Peace, President Tokayev has committed to contribute to the stabilization of Gaza by supporting civilian reconstruction, ensuring food security, and providing digital government solutions. Kazakhstan's peacekeepers in UNDOF and UNIFIL reflect our readiness to assume practical responsibility and contribute to the international mandated stabilization forces in Gaza. Kazakhstan formally announced its intention to join the Abraham Accords. We see them as an additional platform to reinforce the UN brokered political process towards the two-state solution. The long-term stability of Afghanistan remains inseparable from the security and sustainable development of Central Asia. Humanitarian assistance remains indispensable, but it cannot by itself break the cycle of poverty, displacement, and dependency. Kazakhstan supports pragmatic, coordinated, and step-by-step international engagement with Afghanistan, with the UN playing the central role. Finally, we have watched with growing concern in recent years the erosion of protection of civilians in conflict zones. In response, together with Brazil, China, France, Jordan, South Africa, and the ICRC, Kazakhstan is advancing the global initiative to galvanize political commitment to international humanitarian law. Mr. President, the growing role of middle powers in global affairs is opening new avenues for practical cooperation to achieve SDGs. Kazakhstan is working with the United Nations to operationalize the United Nations Regional Center for the Sustainable Development Goals for Central Asia and Afghanistan in Almaty City. Its success should be measured by what it delivers. I thank my colleagues, the foreign ministers of Central Asia, for helping shape a practical and focused agenda for the center. Reaffirming our commitment advancing primary health care as the cornerstone of universal health coverage, we call upon the UN member states to join the Global Coalition on Primary Health Care. 2026 has been designated by this body as the International Year of Volunteers. for sustainable development. This initiative, originally at President Tokayev's suggestion, has given new impetus to volunteerism as a force for stronger communities, youth engagement, and environmental action. In Kazakhstan and elsewhere, hundreds or thousands of people have joined volunteer activities. Excellencies, environmental challenges are among the defining issues of our time. Climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation, and the growing frequency of natural disaster are placing increasing pressure on our societies and economies. The Regional Ecological Summit held in Astana in April reaffirmed that climate, water, food, and health challenges cannot be addressed in isolation. Its declaration, Environmental Solidarity of Central Asia, provides a strong foundation for advancing regional cooperation on environmental protection and sustainable development. On the same day, the heads of states of the founding countries of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea declared an International Day of Aral Sea and Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers with the aim of raising global awareness of the region's environmental challenges and mobilizing greater international support for their preservation. We are grateful for the support of UN member states and partners for President Tokayev's proposal to proclaim 22nd April as the International Day of Greening of the Planet, aimed at amplifying global efforts to restore ecosystem. Kazakhstan pursues a human-centered approach to contemporary challenges emphasizing peacebuilding, dialogue, and cooperation as an essential response to the complex global challenges of our time. This approach is underpinned by a broader mental shift toward environmental stewardship, civic engagement, and care for the public good. It's reflected in nationwide efforts to improve public spaces, advance large-scale greening, and promote the values of respect for the rule of law, active and responsible patriotism, volunteerism, and compassion as integral elements of everyday life and civic culture. This brings us to another critical topic of our day. Healthy ecosystems depend on water. Water security is fundamental to the well-being and the resilience of our societies. Water underpins public health, food and energy security, climate resilience and peace. Yet, despite its fundamental importance, global water governance remains fragmented. The recent devastating floods in the mountainous regions of Nepal and China remind us of the growing risk associated with water and climate-related disasters. In this context, President Tokayev has proposed the establishment of an international water organization under the auspices of the United Nations. The purpose is to make international water governance more coherent, accountable, and capable of effective implementation. Kazakhstan calls for inclusive member state-led process to explore options for strengthening the institutional architecture for water within the United Nations. These risks are particularly serious in the military domain, where the use of AI in warfare, and cyber operations could have far-reaching consequences for international stability. Kazakhstan supports stronger international rules and cooperation, including through the United Nations Global Mechanism on ICT security and UN Global Dialogue on AI governance. At the regional level, we invite partners to engage with the UNISCAP Asia-Pacific Digital Solutions Center in Almaty City as a platform for sharing expertise and advancing regional digital cooperation. Ladies and gentlemen, one thing is clear. There is a global trust deficit. Restoring trust will take time. But greater trust will not just appear like magic. It's a result of increasing, not decreasing, international cooperation. And we must build it. The system of international cooperation we call multilateralism, in whose famous hall we stand today, depends on us, just as we depend on it. through the institution of multilateralism, must deliver tangible benefits, but equally true, we, the Member States, must honor our commitments, adhere to global standards, and work together. Kazakhstan will remain a reliable partner for peace, security, and sustainable development. We will continue to choose cooperation over coordination and work with all Member States to strengthen the United Nations and turn our shared commitments into meaningful action. And I thank you. I thank you.

Turning to education, reforming this sector is the basis of our effort to provide high quality education that provides equal opportunities and ensure equity. Turning to good governance, We focus on transparency, the independence of the judiciary and combating corruption while reforming public offices and promoting investment. Our approach addresses the hiking prices, confronting any threats to the security or terrorism, while tackling also vulnerability and poverty. The complementarity between all those dimensions ensured our country's security and stability in an environment full with disruptions. Mr. President, Mauritania adopts a balanced approach that covers all our inheritances, be it African, Islamic, Arab and others. We are guided by our foreign policy underpinned on cooperation, solidarity and the respect of sovereignty and good neighborliness. Proceeding from the above, we believe that confronting the common challenges necessitates promoting multilateralism. We need the concerted effort of the international community. In a practical translation of such effort, my country, through its participation in the different events and peacekeeping missions, contributes in the peaceful settlement of disputes and promoting cooperation and coordination, both regionally and internationally. This contribution is based in our belief in the need to have durable and just cooperation, because no one country, no matter how powerful it was, can stand alone to confront the challenges of such an interconnected world. However, the high influx of migration and their complexity reveals the reality that should be analyzed without any exaggerations. and it should also preserve the unity of societies. We need an effective response to this challenge through cooperation between the countries of origin, transit, and destination. We have to ensure a fair share of the responsibilities and burdens and address the root causes of irregular migration while combating human trafficking. and smuggling. To contain such influxes and ensure at the same time the dignity of migrants and their rights. The solution is in our common responsibility and solidarity. Mr. President, the expanded theatre of conflicts and the escalating humanitarian cost of such conflicts requires greater protection of civilians while ensuring the peaceful settlement of such disputes for the sake and benefit of communities.
